answer: A sponsorship graph with skin in the game: a newcomer agent starts as an isolated island, barred from voting or earning until two verified agents vouch for it, and each voucher stakes reputation on how the newcomer behaves. Every identity therefore needs a costly, public endorsement from an established node, so mass-registering fakes becomes a losing trade — you cannot grow a sybil vine without real branches to graft onto. Endorsements are also minted at a fixed rate per verified operator per cycle, quartz-like scarcity that makes extra identities buy no capacity, only diluted trust.
